one_line_bio: A men's grooming D2C brand that has turned its feed into a daily meme channel: huge reel reach, but likes and comments that stay thin for a 389K account.
account_summary: Bombay Shaving Company posts almost every day (8.4 posts a week across the last 120 posts, never more than 3 days apart), and 90% of the feed is reels. Reach is the strength: reels average 1.47M views, about 3.8× the follower count, so the algorithm is pushing them well beyond followers. Engagement is the weak spot. Average ER is 0.48%, and the median post sits at only 0.13%, because a handful of breakout reels (one at 23.5M views and 31.6K likes) carry the average. ER over the last 30 days fell to 0.20%, from 0.66% in the 30 days before.
niche: Men's grooming: razors, trimmers, hair removal and perfumes (via @PerfumesByBSC)
target_audience_guess: Indian men aged 18–34 who follow meme and creator culture, plus a smaller group drawn in by the founder and podcast content
brand_voice: Irreverent and meme-first Hinglish ("bruv", "bhaaiii", "Khul Ke Khel"), with very short captions (54 characters on average) and almost no hashtags (0.1 per post)

hook_analysis: Most reels rely on a meme caption with no setup ("Samajh aaya?", "Go with the Blo") and assume the video's first second does the work. That brings reach but gives viewers no reason to like, comment or connect the reel to a product. The hooks that convert open with a personal stake or a question: "I shaved off my beard after 16 years. Here's why", or a Science ya Scam claim like "Can you trust viral hacks…?"
posting_behaviour: Posts are very regular: daily, sometimes twice a day, mostly at 6–7 PM IST (75 of 120 posts). Sunday posts average 1.39% ER against 0.15–0.58% on other days, and the few posts at 3–4 PM (8 posts) average 1.1–2.8% ER. The 6 PM slot, where most content goes, averages only 0.25%.
what_works: Reach: reels average 1.47M views, about 3.8× followers, so the algorithm is pushing them well beyond the follower base
Founder-led launch content (Switch 4) gets 0.88% median ER, 6× the account median
Science ya Scam can break out: one episode got 59.7K likes and 1.76M views
Celebrity podcast clips (Zakir Khan, Bassi, Munawar) reliably reach 1.8M+ views
Consistency: no gap longer than 3 days in 3+ months
what_doesnt_work: Engagement depth: 0.13% median ER is weak for 389K followers, and the 30-day trend fell from 0.66% to 0.20%
Meme reels with no product link get views but don't build the brand. Many could belong to any meme page
Giveaway image posts get 0.11% ER and pull the audience to @PerfumesByBSC instead of this account
Posting at 6 PM, where most content goes, is one of the weakest slots
Captions and hashtags do almost nothing: 54 characters on average and no search keywords
gaps_and_opportunities: Product isn't integrated into the memes. A product-in-the-punchline format would turn reach into recall
Science ya Scam has no fixed slot, episode number or series cover, so the breakout episodes don't build a following
Comments are rarely prompted in reels. Only giveaways ask for them
There are almost no carousels, though how-to and comparison carousels drive saves and shares in grooming
Founder content works but appears only during launches

recommendations.title: Put the product in the punchline
recommendations.why: 76% of posts are memes with 0.14% median ER and little brand recall.
recommendations.how: Keep the meme format, but make the BSC product the twist or the payoff in the last 3 seconds.

recommendations.title: Make Science ya Scam a weekly show
recommendations.why: It produced the account's biggest hit (59.7K likes), but the episodes are scattered.
recommendations.how: Run it every Sunday at 4 PM with an episode number, a fixed cover style and a "vote: science or scam?" comment prompt.

recommendations.title: Move key posts to Sunday and 3–4 PM
recommendations.why: Sunday averages 1.39% ER and 4 PM averages 2.8%, against 0.25% at 6 PM.
recommendations.how: Shift the 2–3 best reels each week into those slots and keep 6–7 PM for lighter memes.

recommendations.title: Founder content every month, not only at launches
recommendations.why: Shantanu-led posts get 6× the median ER.
recommendations.how: Run a monthly "founder answers comments" reel and a behind-the-product story.

recommendations.title: Rethink giveaways
recommendations.why: They score 0.11% ER and send followers to another account.
recommendations.how: Run giveaways as reels on this account, with a product demo and a comment question.

recommendations.title: Add saveable carousels
recommendations.why: Carousels are 1% of posts, and grooming guides are what people save.
recommendations.how: Post 1 a week, such as a "beard style by face shape" or "razor vs trimmer" comparison.

posting_plan: Keep the daily rhythm, but plan it: Sunday 4 PM Science ya Scam episode; 2 product-twist memes; 1 founder or podcast clip; 1 saveable carousel; the rest light memes at 7 PM. Move giveaways into reels with a product demo.
sales_pitch_summary: Your reels already reach far beyond your followers, averaging 1.47M views on a 389K account, but most of that reach doesn't turn into engagement or brand recall: the median post gets 0.13% ER, and the last 30 days fell to 0.20%. The formats that convert are the ones you post least: founder-led launches (6× the median), Science ya Scam, and celebrity podcast clips. We would put the product into the punchline of your memes, turn Science ya Scam into a fixed Sunday show, and move key posts into the slots where your audience responds best (Sunday, 3–4 PM).
